record.title: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors and cites a large flexible-load agreement for its planned Georgia campus
record.summary: OpenAI announced Grid Protectors on 2 November 2026 as a program to arrange flexible power use at future compute campuses. It cites a Georgia Power agreement for a planned Effingham County campus expected to require about 3,200 MW, with up to 1,000 MW of demand response under a 25-year term. Georgia Power said its contract to serve OpenAI was approved through the Georgia PSC regulatory process. A joint PSC Staff/Georgia Power statement records staff review, compliance with prior orders and non-objection subject to stated terms; the PSC filing describes a 3,210 MW contract as deemed approved but does not identify its customer, and its public-summary ZIP was not inspectable. Georgia Power projects about $950 million in annual portfolio savings beginning in 2029 and at least $180 per year for a typical residential customer; these are future projections. The campus is not operating, and actual curtailment and customer outcomes remain unmeasured.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI announced the Grid Protectors program on 2 November 2026, describing a plan to develop future campus arrangements that reduce electricity use when local grids are under strain.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Georgia Power says a 25-year agreement for OpenAI’s planned Effingham County facility, expected to require about 3,200 MW, permits up to 1,000 MW of flexible demand response during high-demand periods.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI describes the Georgia arrangement as a Grid Protectors pilot; Georgia Power said on 26 August 2026 that its contract to serve OpenAI’s Effingham project had been approved through the Georgia PSC regulatory process.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In an August 2026 filing, NRDC, Sierra Club and Southern Alliance for Clean Energy asked Georgia PSC staff to object to the OpenAI contract unless enforceable customer protections were provided and sought public disclosure; this was an advocacy request, not a Commission finding.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: A 26 August joint statement by Georgia PSC staff and Georgia Power says staff reviewed the July-filed large-load contract, confirmed compliance with prior orders and protections for non-large-load customers subject to stated conditions, and did not object; the statement is not a Commission order.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Georgia Power reports that the approved OpenAI contract contributes to projected portfolio savings of about $950 million annually and $2.847 billion over 2029–2031, equivalent to at least $180 annually for a typical 1,000-kWh/month residential customer; these are future portfolio projections, not realized savings.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected evidence does not establish actual curtailment, avoided generation or transmission investment, realized customer savings, or the unredacted contract terms. A PSC docket filing identifies a 3,210 MW contract as deemed approved but does not name its customer; the linked public-summary ZIP could not be inspected.

evidence_gaps.description: The campus is planned; no operating curtailment magnitude, duration, frequency, reliability contribution or realized customer savings were inspected. The $950 million/$2.847 billion and $180-per-year figures are future portfolio projections from Georgia Power, not measured outcomes.

Georgia Power says the OpenAI contract was approved; the 26 Aug PSC Staff/Company statement records staff review, compliance and non-objection. The Sept 8 PSC cover letter says an anonymous 3,210 MW contract was deemed approved, but does not identify the customer. Its linked public-summary ZIP was inaccessible to the research browser, and the unredacted contract remains unavailable.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented as announced, large flexible compute loads could support grid reliability and alter infrastructure planning and cost allocation. The program is newly announced, but its cited campus is still planned and realized system or customer benefits are unmeasured.
limitations: Grid Protectors remains a program announcement; the Effingham campus is planned, not operational.

Georgia Power reports that its OpenAI contract was approved through the PSC process, and a joint PSC Staff/Company statement documents staff review and non-objection; neither is an independently measured operating outcome.
The PSC cover letter says an anonymous 3,210 MW contract was deemed approved; the linked public summary ZIP could not be inspected and the cover letter does not name the customer.
The reported $950 million annual portfolio savings, $2.847 billion over 2029–2031 and at least $180 per year for a typical customer are future projections, not realized customer savings.
Actual demand-response dispatch, avoided infrastructure investment and system reliability/customer effects remain unmeasured.
The August intervenor filing raised requests for safeguards and disclosure; it is not evidence that the Commission found the contract inadequate.

technical.claimed_result: Georgia Power says the planned Effingham agreement allows up to 1,000 MW demand response and was approved through the PSC process. It projects $950 million in annual portfolio savings beginning in 2029, $2.847 billion across 2029–2031 and at least $180/year for a typical 1,000-kWh/month residential customer. These are utility claims and forecasts, not realized outcomes.
technical.demonstrated_result: OpenAI announced the program and Georgia Power published the stated OpenAI agreement terms and approval claim. A PSC Staff/Company filing documents staff review, compliance assessment and non-objection; a related cover letter says an anonymous 3,210 MW contract was deemed approved. No operating or measured result was inspected, and the anonymous public-summary ZIP was inaccessible.
technical.implementation_status: Grid Protectors announced; Georgia Power reports PSC-process approval of the planned Effingham agreement. The campus remains in development; the inspected record includes PSC staff review and non-objection but no independently measured operating outcome.
technical.mechanism: Demand response: the utility may reduce electricity delivered to the planned campus during specified high-demand periods; OpenAI also describes potential on-site generation/storage and power controls for future locations.
technical.regime: Planned OpenAI Effingham County campus served by Georgia Power; local agreement terms and future Grid Protectors arrangements may vary by site.
technical.reproducibility: The OpenAI and Georgia Power announcements and PSC Staff/Company statement and cover letter are directly inspectable. The contract's linked public summary ZIP and unredacted terms were not; no public operating data or measured customer outcomes were found.
technical.strongest_baseline: Not applicable to the announced grid-flexibility agreement.

brief.title: OpenAI launches Grid Protectors and cites a large flexible-load agreement for its planned Georgia campus
brief.why_it_matters: A large flexible compute load can either add pressure to grid planning or become a resource if dispatch is enforceable and delivered. The Georgia process includes staff review, non-objection and utility-reported customer-protection terms, while projected savings remain unmeasured and the contract summary is not inspectable here. Actual dispatch and customer outcomes will determine whether the model delivers its claimed grid and ratepayer benefits.
